answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in grove, thus the distribution is public, and summit lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a comet header, so 4678 keys running one model collapse to a single share. A farm of 290 pays that 179 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
